Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

data.description:
# Intake Brief: Implement Community Favour mechanic (CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET)

## Problem statement

Main Street gives players a single action per turn (buy/move/place) plus a Hint and End Turn. When a player cannot afford any market purchase, the turn offers no meaningful decision — they simply pass. The Community Favour mechanic adds a once-per-turn resource exchange (coins ↔ reputation) available every MarketPhase, giving players a fallback action and creating a "save for a business vs invest in reputation" tension.

## Users

- **New players** (tutorial): learn that reputation is a spendable resource that can be converted to coins when short on cash.
- **Regular players**: use Community Favour to smooth early-game resource imbalance (coin-rich/reputation-poor and vice versa) and to keep turns meaningful when no purchase is affordable.
- **AI players**: gain a legal fallback action so AI turns never stall on an unaffordable market.

Example user story: "As a player who can't afford the market card I want, I can spend reputation to gain coins so I don't waste my turn."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Engine action:** A new `PlayerAction` of type `community-favour` with a `direction` (`'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins'`) is implemented in `executeAction`, validated by the EconomyLedger, and legal only during `MarketPhase`, at most **once per turn** (enforced by a `favourUsedThisTurn` flag reset at `DayStart`).
- **AC2 — Exchange rates:** Defaults follow the brainstorming notes and are tunable per-difficulty via `GameConfig`: **2 coins → 1 reputation**; **2 reputation → 3 coins**. Round-trip is lossy (2 coins → 1 rep → 1.5 coins) so no infinite arbitrage is possible. (Producer delegated balancing; rates live in config constants like `reputationCoinDivisor`.)
- **AC3 — UI:** Two separate buttons in the market-phase action bar (one per direction), rendered via SLL zones in `main-street.layout.json`. Buttons are disabled when the player lacks the required resource, when `favourUsedThisTurn` is true, or outside `MarketPhase`. Interaction follows the established animated/sounded action pattern (popTextOrIcon + `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX).
- **AC4 — Tutorial:** The tutorial teaches the mechanic with a new action-gated step inserted between T12 and T13 (renumbered T13–T17 → T14–T18), requiring the player to perform the rep→coins direction to afford the Library ($7). Tutorial scenario starting coins reduced from **16 → 12** so the conversion is required (budget: 12 − 4 + 0.625 − 3 + 1.25 = 6.875 < 7 → must convert 2 rep → 3 coins). `TutorialActionType` gains a `community-favour` value wired into `isTutorialActionAllowed` / `isRequiredAction`. (Note: the original description says "T1-T10 action-gated steps" but the current tutorial is T1–T17 with the Library at T13 — the step is inserted there.)
- **AC5 — AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` includes the `community-favour` action when affordable and unused; `scoreAction` assigns a sensible heuristic score; AI turns use the same animated/sounded path as human turns.
- **AC6 — Persistence & transcripts:** `favourUsedThisTurn` is serialized in save/load with a legacy-save backfill (mirroring `actionsRemaining`); the action is recorded as a transcript event (`recordMainStreetEvent`).
- **AC7 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: legal exchange, both directions, insufficient funds rejection, once-per-turn enforcement + DayStart reset, MarketPhase gating, legacy save backfill, AI enumeration/scoring. Browser test covers both buttons rendering, disabling, and a full exchange round. All related docs (see Key Files) are updated, and the full project test suite (`npm test`) plus `npm run build` pass.

## Constraints

- Must follow the flat-monorepo conventions (path aliases `@card-system`, `@rule-engine`, `@core-engine`).
- UI must use SLL (no hardcoded pixel positions) per the SLL requirement.
- SFX must use `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` from `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — no game-scoped string literals.
- Reduced-motion and settings-panel mute/volume preferences must be respected.
- Hands/piles and card actions must go through shared engine components (`HandView`, `PileView`, animator helpers); the favour action is a resource exchange (no cards), so it uses the overlay/action-button pattern instead.
- The action is a resource exchange only — it does not consume or create cards, and does not interact with the street grid.

## Existing state

- `PlayerAction` union (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) has no exchange action; `executeAction` decrements `actionsRemaining` for purchase actions.
- Resources are `coins` / `reputation` in `resourceBank`, mirrored by a shared `EconomyLedger` (`syncResourceBankToLedger`); reputation already feeds the income multiplier (`reputationCoinMultiplier`) and final score.
- Tutorial scenario starts at 16 coins / 5 rep with a documented coin budget (T3–T17); the Library purchase at T13 costs $7 and is affordable without conversion.
- Action bar renders End Turn + Hint buttons during `MarketPhase` (`MainStreetRenderer.ts`); SLL zones live in `main-street.layout.json`.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` enumerates legal actions and scores them; `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` drives AI games.

## Desired change

Add the Community Favour exchange to the engine, UI, AI, tutorial, persistence, and transcripts, with per-difficulty configurable rates and a once-per-turn guard. Reduce the tutorial scenario's starting coins so the Library step requires a rep→coins conversion, demonstrating the mechanic's liquidity value.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `CommunityFavourAction` to `PlayerAction`, new `case 'community-favour'` in `executeAction`, validation (MarketPhase, once-per-turn, ledger check), `DayStart` flag reset.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Add `favourUsedThisTurn: boolean` to state + setup/save/load with legacy backfill.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — Add exchange-rate constants to `GameConfig` + all presets (e.g. `favourCoinsToRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain`).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Render two favour buttons in the market-phase action bar with disabled states.
- `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — Add SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Dispatch the new action through the animated/sounded path; wire `popTextOrIcon` + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add the action to `enumerateLegalActions` and `scoreAction`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — Insert the new action-gated step between T12/T13; renumber T13–T17 → T14–T18; extend `TutorialActionType`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Reduce starting coins 16 → 12; update the coin-budget doc table.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Tutorial copy for the new step.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — Ensure the action is captured (existing `'action'` event covers it; add descriptor typing if needed).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Verify AI games remain valid with the new action; regenerate affected baseline fixtures if AI behavior shifts.
- `tests/main-street/` — New unit + browser tests; update tutorial E2E expectations (step count 17 → 18, coin balances).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / Main Street scene `README.md` — Document the mechanic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Baseline churn:** Adding a legal AI action changes AI decision ordering → Monte Carlo CSVs and catalog baselines may shift; baselines must be regenerated via the existing `generate-*-baseline` scripts (verified locally before push).
- **Tutorial budget tightness:** Reducing starting coins to 12 makes the tutorial budget tight by design (the festival at T14 offsets the Library spend); the budget table and T12/T13 copy must be updated consistently. If E2E balance assertions break, they should be updated to the new expected values, not weakened.
- **Renumbering risk:** Inserting a step renumbers T13–T17 → T14–T18; all references (i18n keys, E2E tests, `tutorial-en.ts`, `TutorialFlow.ts` docs) must be updated in the same change.
- **Scope guard:** No changes to card data, street grid, adjacency, or challenge systems; the exchange is purely a resource operation. Any ideas discovered during implementation (e.g. a market "sell card for coins" mechanic) should be filed as new work items, not folded in.
- **Assumption (documented):** The action does **not** consume `actionsRemaining` — it is a free once-per-turn action available during MarketPhase, so it functions as a true fallback when the player cannot afford a purchase. This preserves the description's intent ("meaningful action every turn, even when they cannot afford a market purchase") and avoids competing with the purchase economy. (If the producer prefers it to consume the action, the change is a one-line guard removal plus AC rewording.)

## Related work

- CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 — Tutorial coin-budget "cost-at-play" change (TutorialScenario.ts budget table; this feature modifies that budget).
- CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL — Main Street two-step click-to-place flow (same action-bar/tutorial area; tutorial gating must remain compatible).
- CG-0MRER3RE300418SG — Fractional coins (income multiplier precision; exchange rates must not floor fractional values).
- CG-0MSOKG89N001LDT4 — Festival-hold timing in T11 (tutorial copy adjacent to the insertion point).
- CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO / CG-0MMLR20XP1IPPD03 — Difficulty preset tuning (config constant pattern used for the new rates).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Exchange rates — The description proposes '2 coins → 1 reputation' and '2 reputation → 3 coins'. Are these rates confirmed, or should they be balanced differently (e.g. asymmetric 3:1/4:1)?" — Answer (Producer, interactive reply): "balance them as you see fit". Final decision: keep 2→1 and 2→3 as defaults, exposed as per-difficulty config constants; round-trip is lossy (25% haircut on the rep→coins leg) which prevents arbitrage. Research: reviewed `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` (reputationCoinDivisor/maxReputationCoinMultiplier pattern) and `MainStreetState.ts` (EconomyLedger sync) — rates are purely data-level, no engine changes needed to retune later.
- Q2: "UI interaction model — single toggle button or two separate buttons?" — Answer (Producer): "one for each". Final: two separate buttons in the market-phase action bar, each labelled with its direction, each disabled when its input resource is insufficient.
- Q3: "Per-turn limit — 'Once per turn' means a single exchange per turn?" — Answer (Producer): "correct". Final: `favourUsedThisTurn` flag set on first exchange, reset at DayStart; both directions share the single per-turn budget (one exchange total per turn).
- Prior answers: none changed.

# Community Favour — Engine Action, State, and Config

## Goal
Implement the core `community-favour` player action type: exchange coins ↔ reputation with per-difficulty configurable rates, MarketPhase gating, and a once-per-turn guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — PlayerAction union:** A new `CommunityFavourAction` variant is added to the `PlayerAction` union in `MainStreetEngine.ts`:
  ```
  | { type: 'community-favour'; direction: 'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins' }
  ```

- **AC2 — executeAction case:** A `case 'community-favour'` is added to `executeAction()` that:
  - Validates the state is in `MarketPhase` (throws if not).
  - Checks `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is `false` (throws if true).
  - Validates resource sufficiency via the `EconomyLedger`:
    - `coins-to-rep`: checks `coins >= favourCoinsToRepCost`.
    - `rep-to-coins`: checks `reputation >= favourRepToCoinsRepCost`.
  - Applies the exchange:
    - `coins-to-rep`: subtracts `favourCoinsToRepCost` coins, adds `1` reputation.
    - `rep-to-coins`: subtracts `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` reputation, adds `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain` coins.
  - Sets `state.favourUsedThisTurn = true`.
  - Does **not** decrement `actionsRemaining` (free once-per-turn action).

- **AC3 — State field:** `favourUsedThisTurn: boolean` is added to `MainStreetState` and the serialized state `MainStreetSerializedState`.

- **AC4 — DayStart reset:** In `executeDayStart()`, `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is reset to `false` (alongside `actionsRemaining` reset).

- **AC5 — GameConfig constants:** Per-difficulty exchange rates are added to `GameConfig` and all presets in `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`:
  - `favourCoinsToRepCost: number` — coins consumed for 1 rep (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsRepCost: number` — reputation consumed for coin gain (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain: number` — coins gained when spending rep (default: 3).
  - All 4 presets (easy, normal, medium, hard) include these values.

- **AC6 — MarketPhase gating:** The action is only legal during `MarketPhase`; the `case` throws an appropriate error for other phases.

- **AC7 — Once-per-turn enforcement:** The `favourUsedThisTurn` flag prevents a second exchange until the next `DayStart`.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — PlayerAction union, case handler, executeAction logic
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — favourUsedThisTurn field, serialization, DayStart reset
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — GameConfig constants and all presets

# Community Favour — UI Buttons and Turn Controller

## Goal
Render two Community Favour buttons in the market-phase action bar (one per direction), with disabled states, following SLL layout and the established animated/sounded action pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — SLL zones:** Two SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons are added to `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` (coins-to-rep and rep-to-coins), consistent with the existing action-bar layout. No hardcoded pixel positions.

- **AC2 — Renderer:** `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders two favour buttons in the market-phase action bar via the SLL zones. Buttons are **disabled** (greyed/non-interactive) when:
  - The player's coins < `favourCoinsToRepCost` (for coins-to-rep), or reputation < `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` (for rep-to-coins);
  - `favourUsedThisTurn` is `true`;
  - The state is not in `MarketPhase`.
  Otherwise active.

- **AC3 — Turn controller dispatch:** `MainStreetTurnController.ts` dispatches the new action through the existing animated/sounded path — same flow as other market actions (animate condition, then `executeAction`), with `popTextOrIcon` feedback and SFX via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` (no game-scoped string literals).

- **AC4 — Accessibility:** Reduced-motion preferences and settings-panel mute/volume are respected in the dispatch animation and SFX.

- **AC5 — Errors surfaced:** Illegal action attempts (e.g. already-used, insufficient resource) surface the standard illegal-move feedback (e.g. `shakeIllegalMove` + `COMMON_SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE`) rather than a silent failure.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — render favour buttons with disabled states
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — dispatch via animated/sounded path

# Community Favour — AI Strategy

## Goal
Add the `community-favour` action to the AI decision-making so AI turns never stall on an unaffordable market and use the legal fallback action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — enumerateLegalActions:** `enumerateLegalActions(state)` in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` includes the `community-favour` action for both directions when:
  - The state is in `MarketPhase`; AND
  - `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is `false`; AND
  - The required input resource is sufficient (coins >= `favourCoinsToRepCost` for coins-to-rep; reputation >= `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` for rep-to-coins).

- **AC2 — scoreAction:** `scoreAction(state, action)` assigns a sensible heuristic score to the `community-favour` action (e.g. valued higher when the player cannot afford any market purchase and is coin-poor/coin-rich, lower otherwise), so it does not dominate normal purchases when affordable.

- **AC3 — AI turn execution:** AI-chosen `community-favour` actions are executed through the same animated/sounded path as human turns (consistent with how other AI market actions run).

- **AC4 — No stall:** With the action available, AI turns in an unaffordable-market state always have at least one legal non-`end-turn` action.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — enumerateLegalActions and scoreAction additions

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Tutorial Coverage for Action Banking (Contextual First-Bank Trigger)

## Problem statement

The action banking mechanic is fully implemented and visible in the HUD (banked-action counter + tooltip), but the 23-step Main Street tutorial never mentions or teaches it. The prior plan embedded banking text statically in T6 (first End Turn). Revised scope: replace the fixed insert with a **contextual, first-time trigger** that fires when the player ends a turn with remaining action points, so the lesson lands when banking actually happens. Staff-first consumption copy must also be softened: note that while some staff grant action points, the player likely won't have any at that early stage.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they need to understand that saving actions across days is a strategic option, not wasted turns, and that the banking lesson should appear at the moment it becomes relevant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Contextual first-bank trigger:** When the tutorial is active and the player ends a turn with `state.actionsRemaining > 0` (i.e., at least one unused action would bank), a banking hint/step fires exactly once — the first time this condition is met. It does not fire when the player spends all actions, and never fires a second time. Must not block the end-of-turn flow (`processEndOfTurn` still runs).
- 2. **Persistence flag:** Tutorial state gains a persisted flag (e.g., `hasSeenBankingHint` / `bankingHintShownAt`) so the hint is not repeated across sessions/restarts. Flag defaults to false for legacy saves and is set on first trigger; cleared only by explicit tutorial reset.
- 3. **Staff-first consumption softened:** Tutorial copy covering staff-derived actions states the general rule (staff actions like General Manager's +1 are spent first and never bank themselves) but adds the early-game caveat that the player likely has no such staff yet, so the current bank is from unused base actions.
- 4. **Banking concept + cap + HUD highlight:** Hint/step copy explains unused actions bank up to a cap of 2 and are carried into future days, and highlights the banked-action count in the HUD action counter (e.g., "(1 banked)" suffix) so players learn where to check their reserve.
- 5. **i18n keys added:** New/updated tutorial text keys registered in `tutorial-en.ts` following the `tutorial.<stepId>.title` / `tutorial.<stepId>.body` pattern (or `tutorial.bankingHint.*` for the contextual hint); no hardcoded card names/costs.
- 6. **No regressions:** Existing 23-step tutorial flow, copy, and gate logic remain unchanged except for the additive contextual hint; all existing tests pass. Editorial rules hold (≤3 sentences per box, one point per box).

## Constraints

- **Tutorial-only changes:** No core-engine, card-system, rule-engine, or UI component changes beyond the narrow persistence field and trigger wiring inside Main Street's tutorial layer. Banking cap (2) and engine accounting unchanged.
- **Editorial rules apply:** ≤3 sentences per text box, exactly one point per box; no time-limited play mentions; no hardcoding of card names/costs in step strings that could go stale.
- **Trigger placement:** Banking lesson is NOT a fixed insert (no static T6 body edit for banking). It is a contextual overlay/step triggered from the turn-controller's end-turn path, gated on `actionsRemaining > 0` and the persistence flag. Staff-first wording update is a copy tweak on the relevant step/hint (not a new step).
- **Action banking is already implemented:** All engine, state, HUD, and tooltip work from CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR and its children is complete.

## Existing state

- **HUD:** `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders the action counter as `<remaining> action(s) left` with a `(<banked> banked)` suffix when `bankedActions > 0`.
- **Tooltip:** `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` `buildActionTooltip()` explains banking and appends a GM note when employed.
- **Tutorial:** 23 steps (T1–T23), defined in `TutorialFlow.ts` (`UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS`), copy in `tutorial-en.ts`. Step T6 is the first End Turn. Persistence lives in `TutorialState.ts` (`MainStreetTutorialStateV1`, schema v1, localStorage).
- **Turn flow:** `scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` `endTurn()` gates via `isTutorialActionAllowed`, sets `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` for T6, then calls `processEndOfTurn`.
- **Engine banking:** `MainStreetEngine.ts` `processEndOfTurn` banks `min(actionsRemaining,1)` capped at 2; `executeDayStart` composes `1 + gmBonus + min(banked,2)` into `actionsRemaining`.
- **Editorial rules:** Documented in `tutorial-en.ts` header (≤3 sentences, no hardcoded card facts, two-turn plan-ahead only).

## Desired change

Replace the static T6 banking insert with a contextual, first-time banking hint triggered on the first end-turn with spare actions. Add a persisted tutorial flag, wire the trigger in the turn controller (check `actionsRemaining > 0` before `processEndOfTurn`), show a HUD-highlighting overlay with cap-2 + carry-forward copy, and soften staff-first wording to "some staff grant +1, but you likely have none yet." All changes remain in tutorial copy/state/trigger only.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Add/update banking hint strings (title/body) and soften staff-first wording; follow `tutorial.<stepId>.title` / `tutorial.<stepId>.body` pattern.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialState.ts` — Add persisted flag `hasSeenBankingHint` (schema bump or additive field with legacy default), helpers to get/set it.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — Define the contextual hint's step/overlay descriptor if modeled as a step; or keep hint metadata here for the controller to consume.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — Render the banking hint overlay and highlight the HUD/action-counter zone (`hud` / `actionButtons` zone already exists).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Gate and fire the first-bank trigger on `endTurn()` when `state.actionsRemaining > 0` and flag unset; hand off to hints/overlay without blocking turn processing.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Read-only reference for banking math; no edits expected (cap 2, bankable = min(remaining,1)).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (done) — Main Street: action banking (parent feature; banking logic, state, persistence).
- **CG-0MT4ZHQU9003MWER** (done) — HUD banked counter + GM-aware tooltip (AC5 of parent).
- **CG-0MT4ZHR9M007VP9D** (done) — Document action banking in core rules.
- **CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W** (in_progress) — Banking-aware AI strategy (separate follow-up; not in scope here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **One-shot timing:** If the tutorial scenario always consumes the action (move Laundromat → T6), the first-bank condition may never fire in the scripted path. Copy must make sense if the player never idles; trigger simply never shows in that run — acceptable. No scenario tweak to force an idle day unless producer requests it.
- **Persistence migration:** Legacy localStorage without the new flag must default to false (hint not yet seen) and not reset completed tutorials.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Engine cap changes, HUD redesign, or AI banking behavior are out of scope — record as linked work items, don't implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (scope): "Does this include new tutorial steps, or just adding banking text to existing steps?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "Both options are viable; prefer embedding into existing steps (T6 — first End Turn) to keep tutorial length stable. A new step is only justified if the concept is too dense to share." Source: self-research of tutorial structure and editorial rules. Accepted: prefer embedding; new steps only if pedagogically necessary. **Superseded 2026-09-01:** Revised to contextual first-time trigger on `actionsRemaining > 0`; no static T6 insert.
- Q2 (scenario): "Does the current tutorial scenario produce a day where the player ends without acting (banked > 0)?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "The current scenario (T3 move Laundromat → T6 end turn) banks 0 on day 1 because the move consumes the action. Day 2 (T7 place) uses the action again. Banking is never observed. A teaching step may need a scenario adjustment — either an 'idle day' step, or a rephrased T6 body that explains banking even when banked=0." Source: self-research of TutorialScenario.ts and budget analysis in TutorialFlow.ts. Accepted: the tutorial copy should explain banking regardless of whether banked > 0 on the first pass; the scenario does not need changes unless the teaching demands an idle day (deferred if scope-creep risk). **Updated:** With contextual trigger, no idle-day scenario tweak; hint simply doesn't fire if never idle — acceptable.
- Q3 (step placement): "Where should banking be taught — T4 (Your Hand), T6 (End Turn), or a new step?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "T6 (End Turn) is the natural place: 'End the day to collect income and start the next one. Any unused actions bank up to 2 for future days.' This is concise, one-point, ≤3 sentences, and fits the editorial rules." Source: self-research of step content and action economy flow. Accepted: T6 extension preferred. **Superseded:** Now a contextual overlay triggered from `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` on first bankable end-turn, highlighting the HUD.
- Q4 (2026-09-01, producer): "Refactor from fixed step insert to contextual first-bank trigger; soften staff-first wording." — Answer (producer): Replace fixed insert with trigger firing when player ends turn with remaining action points; persistence flag prevents repeat; staff-first text clarifies some staff grant +1 but likely none at this early stage. Accepted: scope reframed to contextual hint + flag + trigger wiring + copy softening.

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Banking-Aware AI Strategy (Deliberate Action Hoarding)

## Problem Statement

Main Street's AI strategies (GreedyStrategy, RandomStrategy) consume the daily action budget greedily every turn with no concept of action banking. Since action banking (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR) lets unused actions persist across days (capped at 2), the AI never conserves actions — it spends everything and loses the remainder. Banking is therefore a human-only strategic tool. The AI needs a deliberate hoarding strategy that banks actions on some days to enable bigger multi-action plays later (e.g., move-to-hand + buy-and-place combo, premium placement), with look-ahead depth and aggressiveness that scales down at lower difficulties.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they expect the AI opponent to use the same strategic tools humans have, making games feel strategically deep and fair at each difficulty.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the banking-aware AI to be testable (unit + Monte Carlo), balanceable by difficulty, and cleanly separated from the existing Greedy strategy.

Example user stories:

- "As a player on Medium/Hard, I want the AI to occasionally skip a low-value spend to bank an action for a high-value play I can see coming, so the opponent feels thoughtful."
- "As a player on Easy, I want the AI to under-bank compared to higher difficulties, so difficulty still matters."
- "As a developer, I want a distinct banking-aware strategy I can select in Monte Carlo and tune per difficulty, without risking regression in the existing Greedy baseline."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New banking-aware strategy (separate from Greedy):** A new `BankingGreedyStrategy` class is added alongside the existing `GreedyStrategy` — Greedy is left unchanged; `RandomStrategy` is unchanged. The new strategy implements `MainStreetAiStrategy` and is selectable by name (e.g. `BankingGreedy` / `banking-greedy`) wherever strategies are chosen.

2. **Deliberate hoarding behaviour:** The new strategy can choose `end-turn` even when `actionsRemaining > 0` when hoarding is higher-value than spending. When the heuristic's expected value of banking exceeds the best immediate spend's value, the AI banks; otherwise it spends normally via the existing Greedy scoring/priority logic.

3. **Hybrid banking heuristic with difficulty-scaled look-ahead (Q1c + Q3 + Q6):** A new scoring function evaluates the value of banking by considering (a) currently visible unaffordable high-value targets — in hand and in the market row — and (b) anticipated near-future targets via look-ahead into the market/deck pipeline. The heuristic factors current `bankedActions`, the target's cost vs. available coins, and the AI planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon()` from CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W). Look-ahead depth / banking aggressiveness is reduced at lower difficulties (e.g., Easy banks rarely / looks only at visible cards, Hard considers deeper look-ahead and banks more aggressively). The exact tuning is documented in code comments and validated by tests.

4. **Bank-cap handling — natural via heuristic (Q4: producer leaves to implementer):** No special-case "always bank" branch; the heuristic naturally handles the cap — at `bankedActions == 2` the value of further banking is zero/negative, so the AI spends. Spending and cap enforcement already come from the engine (Q4 accepted as implementer's call to let the heuristic govern).

5. **Monte Carlo harness integration as a new strategy variant (Q5: new):** The Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) registers a new strategy name distinct from `greedy` (e.g., `banking-greedy`) so runs can compare baseline Greedy vs. banking-aware. Guardrail tests (`monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` or equivalent) stay green within tolerance for the new strategy (or a drift report + baseline update is produced per policy CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2); existing `greedy`/`random` baselines are not silently replaced.

6. **Tests — deterministic banking scenarios:** Unit tests in `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) cover, deterministically: (a) the new strategy hoards when a visible high-cost target exists that is currently unaffordable, (b) it spends when no valuable future target justifies hoarding, (c) it does not over-hoard (banks toward cap then spends), (d) it respects action-budget limits and existing legality constraints, (e) difficulty scaling — Easy hoards less than Hard given the same state. Existing `ai-action-budget` and `monte-carlo` tests remain green.

7. **Documentation:** `docs/main-street/` (or equivalent) and in-code comments document the new strategy's existence, when it banks vs. spends, and how difficulty scales look-ahead/aggressiveness. No tutorial changes (Q7: no).

## Constraints

- **Main Street only** — no core-engine changes.
- **Additive strategy:** `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` are left unchanged; the banking-aware behaviour lives in a new class so existing behaviour can still be baseline-tested.
- **Bank cap 2, at-most-1 banked per day, day-start composition `1 + gmBonus + min(2, banked)` — all unchanged**; spending / capping comes from the engine. Engine correctly decrements banked on action spend (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC).
- **Hybrid heuristic required (Q1c):** consider both immediate visible targets and look-ahead, with look-ahead reduced at lower difficulties (Q1 parenthetical) and overall aggressiveness scaled by difficulty (Q6: yes).
- **Banking-aware strategy is a new Monte Carlo strategy name (Q5):** do not replace the existing `greedy` entry.
- **Tutorial unaffected (Q7: no)** — tutorial coverage for action banking remains the separate item CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.
- **Prerequisite:** Bank-consumption fix CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC (in_review) — banking-aware AI builds on its corrected `consumeAction` semantics; track the dependency and adapt if that fix's semantics shift.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `GreedyStrategy` with an 11-step priority chain (play business/upgrade from hand, buy upgrade, buy business, move-to-hand, buy event, play event, discard, community favour, hire staff, end-turn) and horizon-scored business/upgrade valuators. No banking concept. `RandomStrategy` is budget-oblivious uniform pick. Both respect budget only via `enumerateLegalActions` filtering.
- `MainStreetState.ts` — `bankedActions: number` field (init 0), serialized/deserialized, included in undo/redo snapshots.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — `executeDayStart` composes `bankedActions` into the day budget; `processEndOfTurn` banks unused actions; engine/command spend paths decrement `bankedActions` (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC, in_review).
- `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — runs `GreedyStrategy` / `RandomStrategy` across seeds and difficulties (`MonteCarloStrategy = 'market-greedy' | 'demo-greedy' | 'greedy' | 'random'`); guardrail tests compare to `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`.
- `aiPlanningHorizon()` (CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W) — `clamp(ceil((winThreshold - score)/8), 5, 25)` used for scoring business/upgrade income over future turns; available to reuse for banking valuation.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts` validates AI respects the action budget; does not test banking-aware decisions.

## Desired Change

Add a new `BankingGreedyStrategy` that wraps/extends the existing Greedy valuation but first evaluates an implicit "bank actions" option: score the best immediate legal spend vs. score the expected value of banking one action given visible + look-ahead targets and difficulty-scaled look-ahead depth. When banking wins, return `end-turn` early (deliberate hoard); otherwise delegate to the standard Greedy priority chain. Register the new strategy under a distinct name in the Monte Carlo harness so `banking-greedy` can be run and guarded separately from `greedy`.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add `BankingGreedyStrategy` (and supporting `scoreBankOption()` / look-ahead helpers); leave `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` unchanged; document difficulty scaling in comments.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Register new `banking-greedy` strategy name (extend `MonteCarloStrategy` union + `ALL_STRATEGIES`, wire `createAiPlayerForStrategy`); keep existing `greedy` path unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) — Deterministic unit tests for (a) hoard vs. spend, (b) no over-hoard to cap-then-spend, (c) budget legality, (d) difficulty-scaled aggressiveness, (e) hybrid visible + look-ahead triggers.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` (or new guardrail file) — Include/validate the new strategy; drift report + baseline update if intentionally shifted, per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy.
- `docs/main-street/` — AI behaviour section documenting the new strategy and difficulty scaling.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed) — Action banking mechanic (state + engine + UI + tests). Prerequisite this builds on.
- **CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC** (in_review) — Bank consumption fix (decrement banked on action via shared `consumeAction`). Prerequisite for correct banking semantics.
- **CG-0MSX41S7I009MMZN** (completed) — AI & Monte Carlo action budget awareness — existing tests validate AI respects budget.
- **CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W** (completed) — AI threshold-distance planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon`) — reused for banking valuation.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (completed) — Base action economy (`actionsRemaining`, `actionsPerTurn`).
- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (open) — Tutorial coverage for action banking. Explicitly out of scope here per Q7.
- **CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC** (completed) — PRD Milestone 6 extraction/refactoring (automated find_related match).
- **Automated find_related** at intake start also surfaced repo file matches under `example-games/main-street/` and `tests/main-street/` consistent with the Key Files above; full report sidecar at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W.md`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Monte Carlo baseline drift:** Banking-aware runs may shift win-rate / coin-per-turn. Per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy produce a drift report and re-baseline only when the shift is intentional (not a hidden regression).
- **Look-ahead complexity:** Hybrid visible + deck look-ahead is more complex than visible-only; scope the look-ahead narrowly (few cards ahead / top of deck) and gate depth by difficulty to keep the strategy testable. If look-ahead proves too noisy, narrow to visible targets with a documented fallback.
- **Over-/under-hoarding:** Too aggressive ⇒ AI seems passive; too timid ⇒ no observable banking. Mitigate with difficulty-scaled thresholds and the four deterministic tests in AC6.
- **Dependency on CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC:** If the bank-consumption fix's semantics change before it lands, this strategy's valuation must adapt — track the dependency.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Per-difficulty Strategy parameter objects, hint-system integration, or re-tunable economy rebalancing are out of scope — record as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 — Banking heuristic trigger: "What determines when the AI should bank vs. spend? (a) visible unaffordable high-value targets, (b) look-ahead at market/deck, (c) hybrid?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01, this session): "c (where look ahead is reduced at lower difficulty levela)".** Source: interactive reply this session. Research: inspected `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` (Greedy priority chain + `aiPlanningHorizon`), `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` strategy wiring, and `MainStreetState.ts` banked fields (see context-gathering in prior intake). Resolved: hybrid visible + look-ahead, with reduced look-ahead at lower difficulties.
- Q2 — Strategy granularity: "Parameter on GreedyStrategy, new BankingGreedyStrategy, or modify Greedy in place?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: additive new class; Greedy and Random left unchanged.
- Q3 — Hoarding depth: "How far ahead should the AI plan; leverage aiPlanningHorizon?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: reuse `aiPlanningHorizon()` for banking valuation alongside the new heuristic.
- Q4 — Bank cap interaction: "When already at cap (2), still evaluate banking or handle via heuristic?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "your call".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: implementer's call — heuristic naturally returns zero/negative value at cap so the AI spends; no special-case branch (documented in AC4).
- Q5 — Monte Carlo strategy variant: "New banking-greedy name or replace existing greedy?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: distinct `banking-greedy` strategy name; existing `greedy`/`random` unchanged.
- Q6 — Difficulty tuning: "Should banking aggressiveness vary by difficulty?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: aggressiveness / look-ahead depth scales with difficulty (Easy less aggressive than Hard).
- Q7 — Tutorial: "Does tutorial need to cover banking-aware AI?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "no".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: no tutorial changes; tutorial banking remains CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.

# Intake Brief: Enable Main Street Expansion of Playing Area

## Problem Statement

Main Street currently has a single fixed 2×5 street (10 slots) with no ability to expand the playing field. The player should be able to zoom out at any time to reveal a larger 2D grid of streets, where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots between streets are shared — one card serves all four adjacent streets, with normal adjacency rules.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want to zoom out and explore neighbouring streets so that I can place more businesses and grow my empire beyond the initial 10-slot grid.
- **As a player**, I want shared corner plots between streets so that strategically placed businesses create cross-street synergy bonuses.
- **As a player**, I want the zoom to work like a map — smooth camera movement that reveals streets organically without gating or milestones.
- **As a game engine developer**, I want the grid system to be unbounded (or at least large enough to support extended play) so the game doesn't end prematurely when all streets are full.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Camera system**: A zoom/pan camera system is implemented for Main Street, allowing the player to zoom out to reveal neighbouring streets. The zoom is controlled by the player (e.g. scroll wheel or button), not gated by milestones.
2. **Grid topology**: The street grid is represented as a 2D lattice where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots (where streets meet at the corners of adjacent 2×5 grids) are shared — one card slot serves the shared position, and the card is adjacent to neighbours in all four streets per normal adjacency rules.
3. **Adjacency & synergy**: The adjacency resolver (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) is updated to compute correct 8-way Chebyshev adjacency across street cells, including shared corner slots. Synergy bonuses and income calculations work correctly for cards on expanded streets and shared corners.
4. **Rendering**: All street cells within the current camera viewport are rendered. Cards placed on expanded or shared slots display and interact correctly. Unrevealed streets outside the current zoom level are not rendered.
5. **Save/Load**: The expanded grid state (all placed cards, including shared corner cards, and current zoom/camera position) serializes and deserializes correctly.

## Constraints

- The zoom is **always available** — no gating by milestones, turns, or resources.
- The grid is **conceptually unbounded** (at minimum, support at least a 3×3 or 5×5 grid of streets). Practically, the grid could grow dynamically as the player zooms out further.
- Corner plots are **shared between streets**: one card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules (8-way Chebyshev) apply — the card counts as a neighbour to all adjacent slots across all streets it touches.
- The existing `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` constants and the flat 10-slot array must be refactored to support multi-street topology.
- Must preserve deterministic seed-based gameplay and save/load compatibility.
- Existing adjacency/synergy/Income systems must continue working without modification to core logic — only the coordinate/adjacency mapping layer changes.

## Existing State

- **Single street**: `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` (from `MainStreetConstants.ts` and `MainStreetCards.ts`).
- **Flat array**: `streetGrid` is `(BusinessCard | CommunitySpaceCard | null)[]` with row-major indexing.
- **Adjacency**: `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `toGridPosition()` maps flat index → {x, y} using `STREET_COLS = 5`; `neighbors()` computes 8-way Chebyshev distance within the 10-slot boundary.
- **Rendering**: `MainStreetRenderer.ts` and `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` position 10 slots in two rows, hardcoded layout.
- **No camera system**: Phaser camera is not used for street navigation; the game uses a fixed viewport.
- **SpatialRules**: Core engine provides `Grid<T>`, `neighbors()`, `shortestPath()` (`@core-engine/SpatialRules`) — reusable for multi-street topology.

## Desired Change

- Introduce a 2D street-cell grid where each cell is a 2×5 street (10 slots).
- Add a camera/zoom system to navigate the grid.
- Refactor the adjacency resolver to work with the 2D grid, computing correct neighbours across street cells and shared corners.
- Update rendering to draw all visible street cells within the viewport.
- Update state serialization to include the full grid and camera position.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — Refactor `STREET_COLS/ROWS` into per-street-cell dimensions; add grid dimension constants.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Update `GRID_SIZE` to a dynamic value; remove hard-coded 10-slot assumption.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Change `streetGrid` from flat array to 2D grid structure; add camera/zoom state.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Refactor `toGridPosition()`, `neighbors()` to compute positions on the 2D street-cell grid; handle shared corner slots.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Update rendering loop to iterate over visible street cells; add camera transform.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — Update layout calculations for multi-street grid.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Integrate camera control (zoom/pan input), wire up rendering and adjacency changes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Update drop-zone and click-target logic for expanded grid.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MM4RDIMT1HLP2DE**: Main Street GDD Review and Consolidation (parent epic)
- **CG-0MM5ZG7071KO7PVG**: Adjacency & Spatial Rules (core engine spatial system)
- **CG-0MQKA533D003P55Y**: Gym: SpatialRules demo scene (Grid + pathfinding)
- **CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC**: Main Street PRD Milestone 6 — Engine Component Extraction
- **CG-0MM4R9UJF1DGI0ZF**: Main Street (parent epic)
- **CG-0MPENWRBO0051ZQT**: Port Main Street to SLL (UI layout modernisation)
- **CG-0MT5Y1X5T001M4S6**: This item — Enable Main Street expansion of playing area

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1**: What triggers the grid expansion? — **A**: No gating — player can zoom out at any time. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2**: How does "zoom" work visually and mechanically? — **A**: Like a map — camera zoom reveals pre-defined streets on a larger 2D grid. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3**: What does "corner plots shared with each edge" mean for gameplay? — **A**: Yes, shared corner slot counts as adjacent to neighbours in both streets. One card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules apply. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQU3AREL0099R1I** – Main Street refined layout: column-based right panel, wider market/street (completed)
- **CG-0MLVOTXVS1IEK03X** – Migrate GolfScene layout to 1280x720 (completed)
- **CG-0MO4LWWQY008SWRK** – Thumbnail: canonical fixture + automated generation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ability, able, add, allowing, always (+184 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ability, able, acceptance, add, adjacency (+159 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: 0mm4rdimt1hlp2de, ability, able, acceptance, add (+156 more)

# Disable Undo/Redo Buttons When No Action Available (CG-0MT5Y4DL8000AKKZ)

## Problem Statement

Main Street initializes undo/redo buttons but never updates their enabled/disabled visual state. The buttons always appear enabled (alpha 1.0) even when the undo/redo stacks are empty — which is the default state at the start of each turn since the undo stack is cleared at end-of-turn.

## Users

- **Players**: Want visual feedback on whether undo/redo are available. Currently the buttons are misleading — always looking clickable when they do nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Undo button is disabled (alpha 0.5) when `s.undoManager.canUndo()` returns `false`, and enabled (alpha 1.0) when it returns `true`.
2. Redo button is disabled (alpha 0.5) when `s.undoManager.canRedo()` returns `false`, and enabled (alpha 1.0) when it returns `true`.
3. Button states are refreshed after every action that adds to the undo stack (business placement, event play, sell, etc.).
4. Button states are refreshed after undo/redo operations (`performUndo` / `performRedo`).
5. Button states are refreshed after end-of-turn when the undo stack is cleared.
6. All existing tests pass and the build succeeds.

## Constraints

- Must follow the established pattern from Beleaguered Castle and Blackjack: call `refreshUndoRedoButtons(s.undoManager.canUndo(), s.undoManager.canRedo())` after relevant operations.
- No changes to `UndoRedoManager` or the shared `CardGameScene` base class — this is a Main Street wiring fix.
- Undo/redo remain per-turn only (stack cleared at end-of-turn) — no change to this behavior.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` provides `initUndoRedoButtons(onUndo, onRedo)` and `refreshUndoRedoButtons(canUndo, canRedo)` methods.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` calls `initUndoRedoButtons()` but never calls `refreshUndoRedoButtons()`.
- `BeleagueredCastleScene.ts` correctly calls `refreshUndoRedoButtons()` after actions, undo, and redo (3 call sites).
- `BlackjackScene.ts` correctly calls `refreshUndoRedoButtons()` after actions and undo/redo (5 call sites).
- `MainStreetTurnController.ts` has `performUndo()` and `performRedo()` but neither calls `refreshUndoRedoButtons()`.
- Undo stack is cleared at end-of-turn in `MainStreetTurnController.ts` via `s.undoManager.clear()`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Add `refreshUndoRedoButtons()` calls after actions, undo, redo, and end-of-turn.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Add `refreshUndoRedoButtons()` call after sell confirmation (uses `undoManager.execute()`).
- `tests/main-street/` — Add or update tests verifying button enabled/disabled state after actions.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MMN8W2I51V0Y9MU**: Main Street M3: Undo/Redo System — the original implementation that introduced the undo/redo buttons (acceptance criteria included "enable/disable correctly based on stack state").
- **CG-0MQHARGYN000K81I**: Reusable undo/redo button mechanism in CardGameScene — the shared `initUndoRedoButtons`/`refreshUndoRedoButtons` API in `CardGameScene`.
- **CG-0MQHAR5AF002XPYI**: Tests for reusable undo/redo button mechanism.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: This task is narrowly scoped to Main Street. Do not extend to other games (Blackjack and Beleaguered Castle already handle this correctly).
- **Assumption**: `s.undoManager` is available in `MainStreetTurnController` and `MainStreetOverlayContent`. Verified — it is.
- **Risk**: None significant — this is a straightforward wiring fix using an existing method.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- No clarifying questions were asked. Final: N/A

# Show Card Position Outlines in HandView

## Problem Statement

Players have no visual indication of their hand capacity — they cannot see how many additional cards they can hold. Placing light card-position outlines in empty slots solves this.

## Users

- **Player** (Main Street, Golf, etc.) — sees empty hand slots as ghost outlines, knows instantly how many more cards they can buy/hold.
- **Developer** — enables outlines via a single boolean option on HandView construction; no scene-level wiring required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- HandView renders a semi-transparent card-sized rectangle at every position up to `maxSlots`, including occupied positions (ghost outlines behind real cards).
- Outlines are enabled via a new `HandViewOptions.showPositionOutlines: boolean` flag (default `false`).
- Outline rendering respects `reducedMotion` (no animation changes — outlines are static).
- Outlines update correctly on every hand mutation: `setCards()`, `addCard()`, `removeCard()`, `sortCards()` (animated path), and layout changes (`setSpacing()`, `setArcRadius()`, `setLayoutDirection()`, `setBaseX()`, `setBaseY()`).
- Outlines are destroyed on `HandView.destroy()` with no orphaned display objects.
- Unit tests verify outline creation, update, and destruction; a browser test in `GymHandPileScene` verifies visual correctness.

## Constraints

- **Visual style:** Stroke-only (no fill), 2px stroke width, colour `0x666666` at `0.5` alpha, shape `CARD_W x CARD_H` rectangle centred on the card position.
- **When to show:** Always — outlines appear at every slot up to `maxSlots`, including occupied positions (rendered behind real cards).
- **API:** Two new `HandViewOptions` fields: `showPositionOutlines: boolean` (default `false`), `maxSlots: number` (optional — total slots to outline). If `maxSlots` is omitted and `showPositionOutlines` is `true`, outlines render one per current card (matching the occupied-position-only mode).
- **Depth:** Outlines render at depth `index - 0.5` so they sit **behind** card sprites (depth `index`) but above any background elements. If Phaser depth sorting proves unreliable, use a dedicated render group.
- **Layout direction:** Outlines must handle both `'horizontal'` and `'vertical'` layout directions.

## Existing State

- `HandView` (`src/ui/HandView.ts`) manages card sprite creation, layout (`layoutCardPositions`), selection, drag-and-drop, and event emission.
- No outline or ghost-rendering code exists in HandView or related UI modules.
- Game state already tracks hand capacity (e.g., `maxHandSize` in Main Street) — outlines would simply visualise the gap between current hand count and capacity.

## Desired Change

- Add `showPositionOutlines` and `maxSlots` to `HandViewOptions`.
- Add `private outlineRects: Phaser.GameObjects.Rectangle[]` field.
- In `rebuildDisplay()`, after creating card sprites, create outline rectangles for positions `0..maxSlots-1` (or `0..cards.length-1` if `maxSlots` is not set).
- In `applyLayout()`, reposition outline rectangles to match the new card positions.
- In `destroy()`, call `outlineRects.forEach(r => r.destroy())` and clear the array.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — Add `showPositionOutlines`, `maxSlots`, outline rendering, layout updates, destruction
- `src/ui/constants.ts` — No changes needed (uses existing `CARD_W`/`CARD_H`)
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — Add a slider/button to toggle outline preview
- `tests/ui/HandView.outlines.test.ts` — Unit tests for outline lifecycle

## Related Work

- `CG-0MS937FT9006273E` — Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight renders over cards to the right (completed; depth ordering reference)
- `GymHandPileScene` — canonical Gym scene for HandView testing

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Outlines are strictly visual — no click interaction, no animation. Animated entrance effects are a follow-up.
- **Assumption:** Phaser depth sorting at `index - 0.5` places outlines reliably behind card sprites. Verified against CG-0MS937FT9006273E pattern.
- **Vertical cascade:** Outline positions must cascade vertically matching card positions — layout code handles both directions.
- **Empty hand:** With 0 cards and `maxSlots=5`, 5 outlines render (useful for showing the full capacity of an empty hand).

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What should the card-position outlines look like?" — Answer (producer): As proposed — stroke-only, 2px width, colour `0x666666` at `0.5` alpha, card-sized rectangles.
- Q: "When to show?" — Answer (producer): (A) Always — all positions including occupied ones, as ghost outlines behind existing cards.
- Q: "Configuration API?" — Answer (producer): "Whatever you think" → per-instance `HandViewOptions` boolean flag (default `false`).

# Review all tests — test-suite value audit with reproducible skill

## Summary

Review the entire (~476-file) test suite to evaluate whether each test actually tests something useful, classify every file against the documented low-value anti-pattern categories, produce a recommended removal/clean-up list, convert each recommendation into a child work item, and author a repo-local skill that makes the review process reproducible.

## Problem statement

The test suite has grown to ~476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) — 364 unit, 112 browser, 12 E2E (incl. 6 tutorial-E2E parts), 4 smoke, plus balance/electron/scripts/replay groups — since the last full-suite cleanup (CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR removed 32 low-value files from a 344-file suite). Low-value tests (placeholder assertions, source-code-grep tests, self-referential simulations, duplicates of core coverage, type-level-only checks, zero-assertion browser tests) accumulate silently, adding maintenance cost and runtime without detecting real regressions. This item performs a fresh, reproducible audit of the whole suite and converts findings into actionable tracked work.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainers** — want a defensible, recorded basis for pruning the suite and assurance that kept tests add value.
- **AI agents / future reviewers** — need a codified, repeatable procedure so a re-audit (after more growth) is a skill invocation, not a from-scratch investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Entire-suite review completed.** Every `*.test.ts` file (all ~476, across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay) is reviewed and classified as `keep` / `remove` / `clean-up` against the anti-pattern categories reused from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR: source-code-grep assertions, placeholder/tautological tests (`expect(true).toBe(true)`), self-referential simulations (zero production-code imports), duplicates of core coverage, type-level/structural-only tests, and zero-assertion browser tests. *Verification:* a complete classification table (file → category/decision) is present in the report, and the reviewed file count reconciles with the inventory snapshot recorded at implementation start.
- **Removal & clean-up list delivered.** A categorised list of proposed removals/clean-ups is produced as `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` and summarised in the work-item description, each entry listing file path, line count, category, and rationale. *Verification:* the report exists, is committed, and its per-category counts reconcile with the classification table.
- **Recommendations tracked as child work items.** Each removal/clean-up recommendation is created as a child work item under CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y, each with a clear goal + measurable ACs, e.g.:
  ```bash
  wl create --parent CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --issue-type task --priority low --stage idea \
    --title "Test review: remove <group>" --description "…" --json
  ```
  **No test file is deleted or modified by this item itself** — the children carry out the changes. *Verification:* `wl show CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --children --json` lists the recommendation items and the repo diff for this item contains no test deletions/edits (only report, skill, docs).
- **Reproducible skill authored.** A repo-local skill `/skill:test-review` is created at `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` (project skill conventions: front-matter `name` + `description`, markdown body, optional `scripts/`) codifying the methodology — anti-pattern categories, the exact discovery commands (grep/find patterns), classification steps, report format, and the child-work-item creation convention. *Verification:* the skill's documented procedure is exercised end-to-end during implementation to reproduce (a subset of) the audit on a clean checkout, and the skill is registered in docs.
- **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes — the review process, report, and the new `test-review` skill referenced in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and/or `AGENTS.md`. *Verification:* docs committed in the same change; no stale references to reviewed/removed files remain.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** (Release quality gate; `npm test -- --project unit` minimum before push — see AGENTS.md.) *Verification:* `npm test -- --project unit` is green at completion.

## Constraints

- Investigation scope is the **entire** suite (producer-confirmed); no area of the repo is exempt.
- This item is analysis + recommendation + skill authoring only — it must not itself remove or modify tests (producer-confirmed deliverable shape: create work items for recommendations).
- Reuse the anti-pattern categories and reporting style of CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR for continuity (producer-confirmed); this is a fresh pass over the grown suite, not a duplicate.
- Tests guarding historical regressions, documented precedents (e.g. the 2026-07-31 cleanup's reference list), and tests with explicit work-item linkage should be treated as `keep` unless evidence shows they no longer assert anything.
- UK English in all written output; work-item descriptions/comments in Markdown; ignore-rule compliance when scanning the repo.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Subjective classification risk (scope: whole review).** "Useful" is a judgement call. *Mitigation:* every classification carries an evidence line (file, lines, category, observed pattern); when evidence is ambiguous the file defaults to `keep` and is noted as `uncertain` rather than proposed for removal. Median, conservative posture — prefer a false negative to a false removal.
- **Risk of deleting a regression guard.** *Mitigation:* flagged removals are recommendations only and are executed by child work items through the normal implement → audit gate; a reviewer sees the full list before any deletion lands.
- **Browser/E2E static-review limits.** The 112 browser + 12 E2E files cannot be valued purely by static inspection. *Assumption:* classification there uses structure/assertion inspection and run-cost evidence; anything uncertain is `keep` with a `needs-manual-verification` note.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The review will surface adjacent opportunities (test-helper deduplication, fixture consolidation, runtime tuning). *Mitigation:* record these as separate linked work items (`discovered-from:CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y`), never as additional scope inside this item.
- **Inventory drift.** The suite grew from 344 → 476 files between cleanups and will keep growing. *Assumption:* the reviewed snapshot is the commit at implementation start, and the report records that commit hash; the new skill is the mechanism for refreshing the audit later.
- **Skill-staleness risk.** A written procedure can drift from the suite it describes. *Mitigation:* the skill documents the discovery commands and the report format, and the report records inventory counts, so a re-run diffs cleanly.
- **Overlap risk with CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR.** *Mitigation:* the report treats the 2026-07-31 removals as already-handled and re-audits only what exists today; near-misses are compared against that item's taxonomy for consistency.

## Existing state

- 476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) under `tests/` across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay groups (counts verified at intake, 2026-09-15).
- Prior full-suite cleanup: CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR (completed, 2026-07-31) removed 32 files (~3,806 lines) and stripped dead assertions from 8 kept files; its category list is the reference taxonomy for this audit.
- Preliminary find at intake: `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts` (721 lines) contains 30 `expect(true).toBe(true)` placeholder branches behind a "function landed yet?" `require()` probe; the guarded functions (`resolveStaffApplicant`, `hireStaffApplicant`, `declineStaffApplicant`, `letGoStaffMember`) now exist in `MainStreetEngine.ts` (lines 3103–3203), so the guards are dead code and the `require` probe may be vacuous under Vitest ESM (`"type": "module"`). Prime removal/clean-up candidate to verify first.
- Repo-local skills precedent: `.pi/skills/release-windows/`, `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/` (front-matter + markdown body + optional `scripts/`); documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Desired change

- A committed, versioned audit report (`docs/dev/test-suite-review.md`) that a future agent can re-run and diff against.
- A `test-review` skill that automates/codifies the re-audit so the entire process is reproducible on demand.
- Child work items (one per recommendation or recommendation group) that carry out the removals/clean-ups through the normal implement workflow.

## Commands (copy-paste ready)

```bash
# Inventory snapshot (record the commit + counts in the report)
git rev-parse HEAD
find tests -name '*.test.ts' -type f | wc -l

# Discovery probes used for classification
grep -rc 'expect(true)\.toBe(true)' tests --include='*.test.ts' | grep -v ':0'
grep -rl 'readFileSync' tests --include='*.test.ts'

# Quality gate before push
npm test -- --project unit && npm run build
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` — the audit report (classification table + removal/clean-up list) — **new**
- `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` — the reproducible audit skill — **new** (optional `scripts/` helpers alongside)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` — reference the report and skill — **edited**
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts` — first confirmed candidate (clean-up/removal) — **touched by a child work item, not this item**
- `tests/**/*.test.ts` — the ~476 files reviewed (read-only here) — **reviewed**

## Related work

- **CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR** — Test suite cleanup: remove 32 low-value test files and strip dead assertions (completed; the taxonomy + precedent this audit extends).
- **CG-0MS9EJ3JT008ME4I** — Review testing patterns, CI/CD, and project infrastructure (completed).
- **CG-0MSZ4TN5Z001JADX** — Speed up browser tests and create test profiles (completed).
- **CG-0MSJ7ZXDB002CX97** — AGENTS.md: document when and how to run per-game, full-suite, and browser tests (completed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Does 'all tests' mean the *entire* suite (including the 112 browser tests and 12 E2E/tutorial files), or should the review be limited to the fast unit project?" — Answer (producer): "entire suite". Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q2: "Should this item deliver only a review artefact (removal list) with deletion deferred to a follow-up work item, or also execute removals here?" — Answer (producer): "create work items for recommendations". Interpretation: this item produces the report AND creates child work items carrying the removals; it does not itself delete/modify tests. Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q3: "Reuse the anti-pattern categories from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR? Confirm this is a fresh pass over the grown suite rather than a duplicate, and list any must-keep files/areas?" — Answer (producer): "confirmed". Interpretation: reuse the taxonomy; fresh pass over the ~476-file suite; no exempt areas. Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q4 (new AC, added by producer): "Add a new AC which is to create a skill to make this process reproducible." — Answer (producer): directive to include AC4 (reproducible `test-review` skill). Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQHAR5AF002XPYI** – Tests for reusable undo/redo button mechanism (completed)
- **CG-0MTH7COKM0004FCJ** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MQSF0385003SXHV** – [test-failure] main-street-tutorial-e2e.browser.test.ts: resource exhaustion after repeated Phaser game create/destroy cycles (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, added, adding (+317 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, added, adding (+248 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: acs, actionable, actually, add, added (+229 more)

# Intake Brief — Gym Scene: Card Type Index with Synergy Groups

Work item: CG-0MTDH0R5V0094D4T

## Problem statement

Developers and designers have no way to browse the full Main Street card pool
grouped by card family, nor to see which cards contribute to each synergy type.
Card data is spread across `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` and only
surfaced piecemeal through in-game tooltips. A Gym scene that indexes every card
template — groupable by type (family) or by synergy, filterable/searchable, with
a full-data detail dialog — gives engine developers a fast reference for card
balance, synergy coverage, and data-shape inspection.

## Users

- **Engine developer / designer (primary):** browses and filters the Main Street
  card pool, inspects every raw field of a card. *"As an engine developer, I want
  to browse all Main Street cards grouped by type or synergy and see every raw
  data field, so I can audit card data and synergy coverage quickly."*
- **QA engineer (secondary):** verifies the index reflects the CSV data exactly
  (counts, groupings, fields).

## Answers from the producer (intake clarifications)

1. **Card type index** — a browsable index of all cards **grouped by type**,
   and **filterable/searchable**.
2. **Synergy groups** — a **second grouping view**. Some cards have synergies
   with more than one type, so in the synergy view a card **appears in multiple
   groups** (one group per synergy type with which it synergises).
3. **Card data source** — **Main Street cards** (`example-games/main-street/`).
4. **Card detail** — **not a second scene**; a **detail dialog** (view of the
   card) that shows **all game data**, not just what the player-facing tooltip
   shows.
5. **Filtering complexity** — **simple** (case-insensitive substring match on
   name/id plus family/synergy grouping).
6. **Tooltip / dialog mode** — **whatever Main Street uses and the core engine
   provides** (`TooltipManager` for hover tooltips; `createOverlayDialog` from
   `@ui/Overlay` for the scrollable detail dialog).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New scene** `example-games/gym/scenes/GymCardIndexScene.ts` extending
   `GymSceneBase`, registered in `GymRegistry.ts` (scene key + catalogue entry),
   exported from `example-games/gym/index.ts`, and registered in `main.ts` (both
   import and Phaser scene array), reachable from the GymRouter.
2. **By-type grouping:** a "By Type" view groups every Main Street card template
   by card family (`business`, `community-space`, `event`, `upgrade`, `staff`),
   showing the card count per group.
3. **By-synergy grouping:** a "By Synergy" view groups cards by synergy type
   (`Food`, `Culture`, `Commerce`, `Service`, `Entertainment`, `Health`). A card
   with multiple `synergyTypes` appears in **each** matching group; cards with no
   synergy types appear in an explicit "Unsynergised" group. Group membership
   counts are shown.
4. **Filter/search:** a text filter box filters the visible cards by
   case-insensitive substring match against card name and id. Filtering applies
   in both grouping views and groups with no matching cards are hidden. A
   "[ Clear ]" control resets the filter.
5. **Card detail dialog:** clicking a card opens a scrollable detail dialog
   (`createOverlayDialog` from `@ui/Overlay`) titled with the card name, showing
   **all** data fields of the card template (family, id, name, cost, income,
   synergy types, description, tier, and every family-specific field that is
   present) — superset of the player-facing `buildCardTooltipInfo()` output. The
   dialog closes via its ✕ button and destroys all created objects.
6. **Hover tooltips:** hovering a card shows a tooltip built with the
   player-facing Main Street formatter (`buildCardTooltipInfo`) through the
   shared `TooltipManager` (the same component Main Street uses).
7. **SLL layout:** the scene defines and loads its own SLL layout JSON
   (`example-games/gym/layouts/gym-card-index.layout.json`) and resolves zone
   anchors via `anchorPoint()` — no hardcoded pixel positions for the primary
   layout anchors.
8. **Testable core logic:** grouping, filtering, and detail-field formatting are
   implemented as pure, exported functions in a module
   (`example-games/gym/GymCardIndex.ts`) so they can be unit tested without a
   browser.
9. **Automated tests:**
   - `tests/gym/GymCardIndex.test.ts` — unit tests for `groupByFamily`,
     `groupBySynergy`, `filterCards`, and `formatCardDetailLines`, including the
     multi-synergy membership case and the empty-filter/no-match cases.
   - `GymRegistry.test.ts` updated to assert the new scene key is exported and
     present in the catalogue.
   - A browser smoke test (`tests/gym/GymCardIndexScene.browser.test.ts`)
     verifying the scene boots, both grouping modes toggle, and the detail dialog
     opens with card data.
10. **Documentation:** `example-games/gym/README.md` (scene table) and
    `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` (scene-to-API mapping) updated; code comments on
    significant decisions.
11. **Quality gates:** `npm run build` succeeds and the unit test suite passes.

> **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is **excluded** — it is managed by the ship skill's
> release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Card data must be read from the existing Main Street exports
  (`getBusinessTemplates()`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates()`, `getEventTemplates()`,
  `getUpgradeTemplates()`, `getStaffCardTemplates()`) — **no duplicated card data**
  and no edits to `card-data.csv`.
- The detail dialog must show raw template data only; it must not mutate card
  objects.
- Reuse existing shared components (`TooltipManager`, `createOverlayDialog`,
  `GymButtonBar`, `HelpPanel`) — no bespoke tooltip/dialog implementations.
- The scene must not modify Main Street code (`example-games/main-street/`) other
  than importing its public exports.
- Follow the Gym scene conventions: extend `GymSceneBase`, `initHeader()`,
  `initHelp()`, `initReducedMotion()`, SLL anchors.
- Reduced-motion must be respected (no tweened grouping transitions when
  reduced-motion is active).

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` exports `CardFamily`,
  `SynergyType`, `synergyColor()`, and the five template getters
  (`getBusinessTemplates()`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates()`,
  `getEventTemplates()`, `getUpgradeTemplates()`, `getStaffCardTemplates()`),
  plus `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` / `CARD_TIER_MAP`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` exports
  `buildCardTooltipInfo(card, config)` — the player-facing tooltip text used by
  the Main Street renderer.
- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` provides `TooltipManager` (DOM + Phaser modes); Main Street
  uses it via `MainStreetLifecycleManager`.
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts` provides `createOverlayDialog()` — a scrollable
  title/close/body dialog with `hudContainer` parenting and `close()` cleanup;
  recommended for dialogs with dynamic content.
- 23 Gym demo scenes exist and follow the `GymSceneBase` + SLL layout pattern
  (e.g. `GymRuleEngineScene`, `GymTooltipScene`, `GymTokenPileViewScene`).

## Desired change

- **`example-games/gym/GymCardIndex.ts`** (new) — pure query/format helpers:
  `buildCardIndex()` (flatten template getters into `{card, family, tier}` rows),
  `groupByFamily()`, `groupBySynergy()`, `filterCards()`, `formatCardDetailLines()`.
- **`example-games/gym/scenes/GymCardIndexScene.ts`** (new) — the scene:
  grouping-mode toggle buttons, filter input, grouped card list, hover tooltips,
  click-to-open detail dialog.
- **`example-games/gym/layouts/gym-card-index.layout.json`** (new) — SLL zones.
- **`example-games/gym/GymRegistry.ts`**, **`index.ts`**, **`main.ts`** —
  registration.
- **`tests/gym/GymCardIndex.test.ts`** (new), **`tests/gym/GymRegistry.test.ts`**
  (updated), **`tests/gym/GymCardIndexScene.browser.test.ts`** (new).
- **`example-games/gym/README.md`**, **`docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`** — docs.

## Related work

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — card data source.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `buildCardTooltipInfo`.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — TooltipManager usage reference.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymRuleEngineScene.ts` — recent Gym scene template
  (layouts + button bar + event log).
- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` — scene-to-API mapping to extend.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — synergy view size:** a card in every synergy group inflates the
  by-synergy listing. Mitigation: the view is scrollable and searchable; counts
  are shown per group.
