# Engine returns pending end-of-turn deltas

Parent: CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q

## Goal

As the presentation layer, I need `processEndOfTurn()` to compute — but not
apply — all end-of-turn resource changes so the scene can apply them once the
closing animations land, while the headless/AI path keeps its current behaviour.

## Scope

Make `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and the ongoing-cost helpers compute
deltas without touching `state.resourceBank`; accumulate them in `TurnResult`;
have the headless/deferred closers apply them so the AI/sim contract and
determinism are unchanged. Keep the competitive (N>=2) paths working.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `applyIncome()` computes and returns `coinDelta` / `repDelta` without mutating `state.resourceBank`.
- [ ] `resolveIncident()` computes and returns `coinDelta` / `repDelta` without mutating `state.resourceBank`.
- [ ] `applyStaffOngoingCosts()`, `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()`, `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()` each return a coin delta without mutating `state.resourceBank`.
- [ ] `TurnResult` gains documented additive fields `pendingCoinDelta`, `pendingRepDelta`, `pendingScoreDelta`.
- [ ] `processEndOfTurn()` sums income + ongoing-cost + incident deltas into the pending fields; `finalScore` is left unchanged until applied.
- [ ] `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` takes the deltas from its context rather than reading already-mutated state.
- [ ] `endTurnHeadless()` and `finishDeferredEndOfTurn()` apply the pending deltas to `state.resourceBank` / `state.finalScore` exactly once, preserving current headless/AI results and determinism.
- [ ] `syncResourceBankToLedger()` is called after application.
- [ ] Competitive (N>=2) income/incident paths still resolve correctly.


### Parent AC Traceability

- [ ] Traces to parent AC1 — Deferred state mutation: `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and any ongoing-cost deductions in `processEndOfTurn()` must not directly mutate `state.resourceBank` or `state.finalScore`. Instead, they compute deltas and return them in `TurnResult` as `pendingCoinDelta`, `pendingRepDelta`, and `pendingScoreDelta` (new fields).
- [ ] Traces to parent AC6 — Headless/AI sims unaffected: `endTurnHeadless()` and the Monte Carlo harness continue to work without change — they bypass the presentation layer entirely. Engine logic (state mutations) still produces the same deterministic results.
## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (applyIncome)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` (resolveIncident, ongoing-cost helpers, processEndOfTurn, runSinglePlayerTurnClosing, finishDeferredEndOfTurn, endTurnHeadless, TurnResult)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` (pending-delta fields if state-held)

## Dependencies

- Tests authored first (child: Deferred end-of-turn mutation tests).

# Scene tracks pre-animation resource values

Parent: CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q

## Goal

As a player, I need the HUD to keep showing my coins/reputation from before the
end-of-turn cycle while the income and incident animations play, so the numbers
change only when the feedback lands.

## Scope

Capture `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` at the start of the end-of-turn
cycle and add an `incidentRevealActive` flag alongside `incomeCollectionActive`
so the renderer knows when the deferred window is open (income + incident).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` are captured from `state.resourceBank` at the start of `endTurn()`, before any animation or delta application.
- [ ] A new `incidentRevealActive` scene flag exists alongside `incomeCollectionActive`.
- [ ] The deferred window is open when `incomeCollectionActive || incidentRevealActive` is true.
- [ ] Both flags are cleared when their animation completes (income collection clears `incomeCollectionActive`; incident cleanup clears `incidentRevealActive`).
- [ ] Reduced-motion / replay / headless paths leave the flags false so no deferral occurs.
- [ ] No regression to the existing `animateHudValueChanges()` delta-pop behaviour.


### Parent AC Traceability

- [ ] Traces to parent AC2 — HUD persists pre-animation values: During the end-of-turn animation window (`incomeCollectionActive` is true or an incident reveal animation is in flight), `refreshHud()` must display the pre-animation resource values (stored as `previousCoins` / `previousReputation`), not the mutated state values. The HUD only updates after the animation completes.
- [ ] Traces to parent AC5 — Reduced-motion mode: When `reducedMotion` is true, there are no animations, so state is applied immediately as before (no regression). The deferred-path is only active when animations exist.
## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` (previousCoins, previousReputation, incomeCollectionActive, new incidentRevealActive)

## Dependencies

- Tests authored first (child: Deferred end-of-turn mutation tests).

## Goal

As a player, while the end-of-turn animations are in flight the HUD must render
the pre-animation coin/reputation values, then switch to the new values once the
animation window closes.

## Scope

- [ ] While `incomeCollectionActive || incidentRevealActive` is true, `refreshHud()` renders `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` (falling back to state when those are null).
- [ ] When the deferred window is closed, `refreshHud()` renders `state.resourceBank.coins` / `.reputation` exactly as today.
- [ ] The score display is consistent with the deferred coin/rep values (no premature score jump during the window) when `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` are available.
- [ ] No visual flicker at the window boundary (a single refresh settles on the correct value; no double-render artefact).


### Parent AC Traceability

- [ ] Traces to parent AC2 — HUD persists pre-animation values: During the end-of-turn animation window (`incomeCollectionActive` is true or an incident reveal animation is in flight), `refreshHud()` must display the pre-animation resource values (stored as `previousCoins` / `previousReputation`), not the mutated state values. The HUD only updates after the animation completes.

# Animator applies pending deltas on completion

Parent: CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q

## Goal

As the presentation layer, I need the income and incident animations to apply the
pending end-of-turn deltas exactly once, at the moment the last animation lands,
then refresh the HUD.

## Scope

Extend `IncomePhaseOptions` (additive, signature-compatible — existing callers
unchanged, per CG-0MTR766U6003RZ88) and `animateIncidentReveal()`'s params with an
optional `pendingDeltas` block; apply on completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `IncomePhaseOptions` gains an optional `pendingDeltas` field; no positional signature change and existing callers compile unchanged.
- [ ] `animateIncomePhases()` applies `pendingDeltas` in the collection finalize step (after the coin-grid flight completes), then calls `updateScore()` / `syncResourceBankToLedger()` and refreshes the HUD.
- [ ] `animateIncidentReveal()` accepts `pendingDeltas` and applies them in its completion `cleanup()` before invoking `onComplete`.
- [ ] Deltas are applied at most once even if a completion callback fires twice (idempotent guard).
- [ ] When `pendingDeltas` is absent, behaviour is unchanged (no mutation; existing tests pass).
- [ ] Reduced-motion mode does not double-apply (the caller applies immediately and passes no pending deltas).
- [ ] Replay/headless mode still fires `onComplete` without mutation.


### Parent AC Traceability

- [ ] Traces to parent AC3 — State applied at animation end: After the income collection animation (or incident reveal, whichever is last) completes, the pending deltas are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` in a single step, followed by a final `refreshHud()` call. The `syncResourceBankToLedger()` is called after this final application.
- [ ] Traces to parent AC5 — Reduced-motion mode: When `reducedMotion` is true, there are no animations, so state is applied immediately as before (no regression). The deferred-path is only active when animations exist.
## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` (animateIncomePhases, collectIncomeGrids, animateIncidentReveal, IncomePhaseOptions)

## Dependencies

- Deferred end-of-turn mutation tests (authored first).
- Engine returns pending end-of-turn deltas.

# Turn controller wires deferred end-of-turn flow

Parent: CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q

## Goal

As a player, I want the delayed state application to complete end-to-end: the HUD
updates only after the closing animations, and the game-over banner never appears
before I have seen the income/incident feedback.

## Scope

`endTurn()` / `finishTurnPresentation()` pass the pending deltas into the
animator, defer `checkEndConditions()` until the animation window closes, and
fall through to the current immediate path when there are no animations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `endTurn()` captures pre-animation values and passes `result.pendingCoinDelta` / `pendingRepDelta` / `pendingScoreDelta` into the closing presentation.
- [ ] `finishTurnPresentation()` passes the pending deltas to `animateIncomePhases()` / `animateIncidentReveal()`.
- [ ] `checkEndConditions()` is evaluated only after all end-of-turn animations complete (or immediately when none run), so the game-over overlay cannot appear mid-animation.
- [ ] When neither income nor incident animation runs, the current flow is preserved (immediate `refreshAll()` + day start; no added delay).
- [ ] Tutorial path unchanged (income show / incident reveal already skipped).
- [ ] Reduced-motion path applies deltas immediately and runs `checkEndConditions()` at the correct point.
- [ ] `syncResourceBankToLedger()` runs after the final application; the day advance happens exactly once.


### Parent AC Traceability

- [ ] Traces to parent AC3 — State applied at animation end: After the income collection animation (or incident reveal, whichever is last) completes, the pending deltas are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` in a single step, followed by a final `refreshHud()` call. The `syncResourceBankToLedger()` is called after this final application.
- [ ] Traces to parent AC4 — Game-over check deferred: `checkEndConditions()` in `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` must NOT evaluate against post-animation state while animations are in flight. It runs after the animation completes (recommended — restructure the closing flow so EndCheck runs after animation, or accept the pending deltas as an optional parameter for the check).
- [ ] Traces to parent AC5 — Reduced-motion mode: When `reducedMotion` is true, there are no animations, so state is applied immediately as before (no regression). The deferred-path is only active when animations exist.
## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` (endTurn, finishTurnPresentation, onEventChoice)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` (runSinglePlayerTurnClosing EndCheck ordering)

## Dependencies

- Deferred end-of-turn mutation tests (authored first).
- Engine returns pending end-of-turn deltas.
- Renderer shows pre-animation HUD values.
- Animator applies pending deltas on completion.

# Design ColorettoRenderer helper module

## Goal
Create `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts` containing all rendering logic extracted from `ColorettoScene`.

## Scope — Methods to extract
- **UI creation:** `createHeader()`, `createLabels()`, `createContainers()`
- **Row rendering:** `refreshRows()`
- **Deck rendering:** `refreshDeck()`
- **Last round card:** `refreshLastRoundCard()`
- **Collections rendering:** `refreshCollections()`
- **Round info:** `refreshRoundInfo()`
- **Layout helpers:** `cardScale()`, `cardW()`, `cardH()`, `rowStep()`, `rowCenterY()`, `rowSlotX()`, `collectionStep()`, `collectionBlockHeight()`, `collectionBlockTopY()`, `collectionBlockBottomY()`, `fixedChipStartX()`, `collectionRowY()`, `displayRowForPlayer()`
- **Card creation:** `createCard()`, `createCardFace()`
- **Label fitting:** `fitNameScoreLabel()`

## Design decisions
- Follow GolfRenderer pattern: constructor takes `(scene, session, replayMode?)` and stores layout.
- Store display objects on the renderer (like GolfRenderer does).
- Use `this.scene` for all Phaser calls; `this.session` for game state.
- Layout constants (CARD_W, CARD_H, ROW_GAP, etc.) stay in the renderer module.
- `refreshModeButtons()` and `destroyModeButtons()` go to the InputHandler (not renderer).

## AC
- New file `ColorettoRenderer.ts` compiles cleanly.
- Scene delegates all rendering to renderer; scene retains `refreshAll()` as thin delegator.
- No rendering logic remains duplicated in scene.

# Design ColorettoInputHandler helper module (extract input from ColorettoScene)

## Goal
Create `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoInputHandler.ts` containing all input handling extracted from `ColorettoScene`.

## Scope — Methods to extract
- **Row click:** `onRowClick(rowIndex)` — validates action, plays sound, dispatches to scene's executeTurn
- **Mode buttons:** `refreshModeButtons()` / `destroyModeButtons()` — create/destroy Place/Take toggle buttons
- **ESC keyboard:** Register ESC handler in constructor, toggle actionMode on keydown

## Design decisions
- Constructor takes `(scene, actionMode, onAction)` where `onAction` is a callback `(playerIndex, action) => void` to delegate execution back to the scene.
- The handler manages the row click zones array internally (creates/removes them).
- ESC handler toggles `actionMode` on the scene and refreshes mode buttons.
- The renderer handles the visual refresh of mode buttons (delegating to renderer for `refreshModeButtons` visual part).

## AC
- New file `ColorettoInputHandler.ts` compiles cleanly.
- Scene wires input handler once in `create()` and delegates row clicks to it.
- ESC toggle, mode buttons, and row click zones all work identically.

# Design ColorettoAiScheduler helper (extract AI scheduling from ColorettoScene)

## Goal
Create `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAiScheduler.ts` (or integrate into existing helpers) containing AI turn scheduling logic extracted from `ColorettoScene`.

## Scope — Methods/logic to extract
- **AI turn dispatch:** `runTurn()` AI branch — phaseManager.set('ai-thinking'), delayedCall, ai.chooseAction(), executeTurn dispatch
- **aiPlayers management:** `sessionToAiPlayers()` — build AI player instances from session data
- **Phase bookkeeping:** `ai-thinking` phase transitions

## Design decisions
- Option A: Extract into a dedicated `ColorettoAiScheduler` class with `(scene, aiPlayers, onAiAction)` constructor.
- Option B: Fold into the InputHandler (since both are about turn flow orchestration, not rendering).
- Option C: Use existing `AiPlayer` pattern from `@ai` module — review if applicable.
- The scheduler's `runTurn()` method is called by the scene after each action completes; it advances to the next player or handles round-over.

## AC
- AI turns execute with identical timing (750ms / 150ms reduced motion).
- `ai-thinking` phase transitions preserved.
- No regression in AI behaviour.

## Notes
- Review Golf's `GolfAiController.ts` for precedent on AI scheduling patterns.
- This is the smallest extraction (~50-80 lines of logic); consider folding into InputHandler or keeping separate based on clean API boundaries.

# Refactor packCoins to left-align coin placements

**Parent:** CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right.

## Goal
Change `packCoins` from centre-relative placement to left-aligned placement so coins start at the left edge of the grid and grow rightwards.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `packCoins` placements start at `w/2` (left edge) and extend to `w/2 + finalGridW - w` (right edge) for X; Y remains vertically centred within the available height.
- [ ] For 1 coin, placement.x equals `w/2` (the first coin sits at the left edge of the grid).
- [ ] All existing packing behaviour (column growth 5→10→15, shrink, overlap, height-fit scaling) is preserved.
- [ ] All placements fit within `availableWidth`: `0 ≤ p.x ≤ availableWidth - coinSize` for every placement.
- [ ] Unit tests updated to assert left-aligned placement values instead of centre-relative absolute values.

## Implementation
- In `packCoins` (coin-grid.ts ~line 202), change the X placement formula:
  - Old: `x: col * (w + s) - finalGridW / 2 + w / 2`
  - New: `x: col * (w + s) + w / 2`
- Update the `packCoins` doc comment to reflect left-aligned packing.
- Update test assertions in `coin-grid.test.ts` that check `Math.abs(p.x) ≤ availableWidth / 2` to check `0 ≤ p.x` and `p.x + coinSize ≤ availableWidth`.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `packCoins` layout formula
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` — placement assertions

## Dependencies
None — this is the first task.

# Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored position

**Parent:** CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right.

## Goal
Change `createCoinGrid` default anchor point and available region so the coin grid renders on the left side of the card instead of the bottom-right quadrant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Default anchorX is at the left edge of the card minus a small inset (`-cardW/2 + leftInset`, default leftInset=8px), so the grid's leftmost coin aligns with the card's left inset.
- [ ] Default anchorY remains at `cardH/4` (bottom quarter of card), keeping the grid in the lower portion.
- [ ] Default `availableWidth` is `cardW - leftInset * 2` (full card width minus left/right insets), giving coins maximum horizontal space.
- [ ] `availableHeight` remains `cardH/2` (same as current default, grid height fits within this).
- [ ] The grid container stays parented to the card and moves with it (existing `createCoinGrid` contract preserved).
- [ ] Existing `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` call (`createCoinGrid(s, card)`) works without modification — defaults are correct.

## Implementation
- In `createCoinGrid` (coin-grid.ts ~line 293), change the default values:
  - `availableWidth = cardW - leftInset * 2` (was `cardW / 2`)
  - `anchorX = -cardW / 2 + leftInset` (was `cardW / 4`)
  - `anchorY` stays `cardH / 4`
  - `availableHeight` stays `cardH / 2`
- Add constants: `COIN_GRID_LEFT_INSET = 8`, `COIN_GRID_BOTTOM_INSET = 12`
- Update `CoinGridOptions.availableWidth` comment: "Region the grid must fit within (defaults to full card width minus left/right insets)."
- Update `createCoinGrid` doc comment: "Defaults: the grid is left-aligned within the card face (`availableWidth` defaults to the full card width minus insets, and the anchor defaults to the left edge)."

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `createCoinGrid` defaults and doc comments
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — verify default call still correct (no per-slot override needed)

## Dependencies
- CG-0MU9JVGNM0051ZVA — Refactor packCoins to left-align coin placements (must complete first)

# Update coin-grid tests and documentation for left-aligned layout

**Parent:** CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right.

## Goal
Update all coin-grid unit tests, browser tests, and VFX-scaling tests to reflect the new left-aligned contract, and update any in-code documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `coin-grid.test.ts` — `packCoins` placement assertions updated:
  - "never clips" test: check `p.x ≥ 0` and `p.x + coinSize ≤ availableWidth` instead of `Math.abs(p.x) ≤ availableWidth / 2`.
  - "shrinks coins" test: check `Math.max(...placements.map(p => p.x)) + coinSize ≤ availableWidth` instead of `Math.abs(p.x)`.
  - "overlap" test: same replacement of absolute-value checks with left-edge checks.
- [ ] `coin-grid.test.ts` — add explicit left-alignment assertions:
  - For 1 coin: `layout.placements[0].x === w / 2` (or within epsilon).
  - For N coins: `layout.placements[0].x === w / 2` and `layout.placements[N-1].x` is the rightmost placement.
- [ ] `coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — update "renders packed coins" test: check icons within left-aligned bounds instead of centre-relative half-extents.
  - Old: `Math.abs(icon.x + grid.container.x) ≤ 70 + 1`
  - New: verify coins are within the card's left-aligned region.
- [ ] `coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — update "never clips: many coins on a small card" test: adjust bounds to left-aligned region.
- [ ] `coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts` — verify no changes needed (pure function, unaffected by layout); if it references packCoins placement values, update accordingly.
- [ ] `coin-grid.ts` header comment updated: "Packing policy: the grid starts at the left edge of the card and grows rightwards (row-major, left→right, top→bottom)."
- [ ] `npm test -- --project unit tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `npm test -- --project browser tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts` passes.

## Implementation
- Update `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts`:
  - Change the "never clips" test from `Math.abs(p.x) ≤ area.availableWidth / 2 + 1e-6` to `p.x ≥ 0` and `p.x + coinSize ≤ area.availableWidth + 1e-6`.
  - Change "shrinks coins" test similarly.
  - Change "overlap" test similarly.
  - Add new test: "coins are left-aligned: first coin at w/2 from grid origin".
- Update `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts`:
  - "renders packed coins" test: replace `Math.abs(icon.x + grid.container.x) ≤ 70 + 1` with left-aligned bounds check.
  - "never clips" small card test: verify coins within left-aligned card region.
- Update `coin-grid.ts` header comment to reflect left-aligned packing policy.

## Key Files
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` — unit test assertions
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — browser test assertions
- `tests/main-street/coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts` — VFX scaling (verify no changes)
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — header comment

## Dependencies
- CG-0MU9JVGNM0051ZVA — Refactor packCoins to left-align coin placements
- CG-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J — Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored position

# Don't mention staff in incidents tutorial step

## Problem

Tutorial step T5 ("Upcoming Incidents") in `tutorial-en.ts` references staff members (the "peek staffer" and "staff grant +1 action") in an explanation that should focus purely on the incident mechanic. This is confusing at the early game stage where the player has no staff yet.

## Users

- **New players** following the tutorial — they haven't hired any staff yet, so staff-related explanations are confusing and out of place.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff references removed from T5 body.** The tutorial step T5 body text no longer mentions "staff", "peek staffer", or staff-granted actions.
2. **Incident mechanic still explained.** The core information about incidents being in a face-down deck, visible count only, and revealed at end of turn is preserved.
3. **Staff comment removed.** The explanatory comment block above T5 that mentions "A peek staff member (staff-lookout) can look at the top card once per turn as an action" is removed.
4. **File is the correct source.** Changes are made to `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts`.

## Constraints

- Only T5 (Upcoming Incidents) is affected; do not change other tutorial steps.
- Preserve the overall tone — instructional, beginner-friendly.
- The staff-related game mechanics are documented elsewhere and don't need to be repeated here.

## Existing state

In `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts`:

- **Comment (lines ~164–167):** `// Face-down incident deck (CG-0MSTOATDP000JNHH): incidents are hidden in a deck — the player sees only the remaining count; the top card is revealed and resolved at the end of each turn. A peek staff member (staff-lookout) can look at the top card once per turn as an action.`
- **Body text:** `'Incidents hide in a face-down deck — you see only how many are left, not what is next. The top card is revealed and resolved at the end of each turn. Some staff grant +1 action (spent first, never banked — but you likely have none yet), and a peek staffer can look at the top card once per turn.'`

## Desired change

- **Comment:** Remove the sentence about the peek staff member; keep the core incident deck explanation.
- **Body:** Remove "Some staff grant +1 action (spent first, never banked — but you likely have none yet), and a peek staffer can look at the top card once per turn." and replace with just the incident deck explanation.

Suggested revised body: `'Incidents hide in a face-down deck — you see only how many are left, not what is next. The top card is revealed and resolved at the end of each turn.'`

Suggested revised comment: `// ── T5: Upcoming Incidents (moved before the first End Turn) ──
// Face-down incident deck (CG-0MSTOATDP000JNHH): incidents are hidden in
// a deck — the player sees only the remaining count; the top card is
// revealed and resolved at the end of each turn.`

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Edit T5 body text and comment

## Related work

- **Tutorial confuses time duration of turn** (`CG-0MTMYIHKO001QCWL`) — related tutorial editing task
- **Easy editing of tutorial text** (`WL-0MTOREREK000A4R9`) — related tutorial editing task

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Only T5 is touched; other tutorial steps mentioning staff are out of scope.
- **Assumption:** The staff mechanics are documented elsewhere (e.g., `specialization-skills.md`) and don't need to be explained in the tutorial.
- **Risk:** If staff peek is a key tutorial concept, removing it entirely could leave a gap — but the user explicitly wants it removed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the instruction is clear: remove staff references from the incidents tutorial step.

```
Unit suite hangs indefinitely. Isolated repro: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/incident-deck.test.ts -t "should return null when the deck is empty"` never completes (killed at 120s). Root cause: the test drains the incident deck with `while (state.incidentDeck.length > 0) { resolveIncident(state); }`. # Decompose MainStreetCards.ts

## Problem
MainStreetCards.ts is 1638 lines, bundling card type definitions, CSV template loading, deck creation, constants, and card utility helpers.

## Goal
Split into focused modules under `example-games/main-street/`:
- `MainStreetCardsConstants.ts` — GRID_SIZE, STREET_COLS/ROWS, WIN_THRESHOLD, STARTING_COINS/REPUTATION, MARKET constants, SYNERGY_BONUS, etc. (<200 lines)
- `MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — All card interfaces (BusinessCard, EventCard, UpgradeCard, StaffCard, CommunitySpaceCard, AnyCard, SynergyType, etc.) (<400 lines)
- `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — CSV loading, template building, getTemplates() accessors, CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES (<500 lines)
- `MainStreetCardsDecks.ts` — Deck creation functions (createBusinessDeck, createEventDeck, etc.) (<300 lines)
- `MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — cardLabel(), getBaseTypeId(), synergyColor(), isDurationEventCard(), isCardAvailableInWeek(), incident helpers (<300 lines)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. MainStreetCards.ts reduced to <800 lines (ideally consolidated to Constants+Types <400 lines since the remaining helpers are pure and simple)
2. Each new module has a single responsibility, documented in a module comment
3. No circular dependencies
4. MainStreetCards.ts re-exports all public symbols from sub-modules (barrel pattern)
5. All existing imports resolve via the barrel — no consumer changes needed
6. Build succeeds (`npm run build`)
7. Main Street unit tests pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/`)

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Source module (1638 lines)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsConstants.ts` — Extracted constants
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extracted type definitions
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — Extracted template loading
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsDecks.ts` — Extracted deck creation
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — Extracted utility helpers
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` — Existing tests that import from MainStreetCards

## Risks
- Low risk: pure data/declarative extraction, minimal behavioral change
- CSV checksum and raw data must be preserved exactly
- CARD_TIER_MAP and CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES must remain accessible
data.title: Decompose MainStreetCards.ts into constants, types, templates, decks, and utils

# Decompose MainStreetMarket.ts

## Problem

## Problem

`implement.py finish` resolves its per-command test timeout from `<cwd>/.pi/test-config.json` (`_resolve_test_timeout`). On TCE that file is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:103 .pi/*`), so it exists only in the main checkout — a git worktree never contains it. The override therefore silently falls back to the 600 s default and the full suite (~15–19 min) is killed mid-run:

```
ERROR: Unhandled exception: Command '['npm', '--silent', 'test']' timed out after 600 seconds
```

Observed while closing the AC5 gap on CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W: `implement.py start` created the worktree, the build and changed-scope tests were fine, then the full-scope gate died at exactly 600 s. Copying `.pi/test-config.json` into the worktree by hand made the intended 1500 s override apply.

## Impact

Every implementation on TCE that runs `implement.py finish` from a worktree hits a hard failure at the mandatory pre-commit test gate — the commit never happens, the item is reset to `open`, and the failure looks like a hanging test suite rather than a missing config file. This is a plausible contributor to the run of failed full-suite attempts (`exit 124`) recorded in `.worklog/cache/` since 2026-09-19.

## Options

1. `implement.py`: read `.pi/test-config.json` from the *owning repository root* (e.g. via the shared worktree/main-checkout resolution already used elsewhere) rather than only the worktree cwd; fall back to cwd.
2. TCE: commit `.pi/test-config.json` (stop ignoring it) so worktrees inherit it.
3. `implement.py start`: copy the untracked `.pi/test-config.json` into a new worktree (mirrors the existing `node_modules` symlink handling).

Option 1 or 2 is preferred; option 3 is the smallest local change but keeps the config duplicated.

## Decision (producer, 2026-09-22)

**Option 2 chosen** — commit `.pi/test-config.json` (stop ignoring it) so git worktrees inherit it. The config is a repo-level fact and belongs in the repository; no cross-repo agent-framework (`implement.py`) change is required. ACs 1–4 below are re-scoped accordingly (the implement.py regression test formerly in AC2 is replaced by a TCE-side tracked/not-ignored/present-in-worktree check; the implement-skill documentation is replaced by `docs/DEVELOPER.md`). See the Appendix for the full question/answer record.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Tracked config.** `.pi/test-config.json` is tracked by git (`git ls-files --error-unmatch .pi/test-config.json` succeeds) and is no longer ignored (`git check-ignore .pi/test-config.json` exits non-zero / reports no match), so a fresh `git worktree` of this repo contains it.
2. **Worktree resolution.** `implement.py finish` in a fresh worktree of this repo resolves `timeoutPerCommand` to the value in the repository's `.pi/test-config.json` (1500), verified by the absence of the 600 s timeout on a full-suite run.
3. **Regression test.** A TCE unit test asserts the config file exists with `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` and is tracked (not ignored) by git — guarding against the file being re-ignored, removed, or emptied.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents that `.pi/test-config.json` is deliberately tracked so git worktrees inherit the per-command test timeout, and explains why (the implement skill resolves the timeout from the worktree cwd).

## Discovered from

CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W (Main Street: banking-aware AI strategy — closing the AC5 Monte Carlo guardrail gap).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MU8PODNT009ML83** – [test-failure] <suite exited 124>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK** – Per-game repos as single-game launchers (blocked)
- **CG-0MTHTJLES009CRHQ** – Linter auto-fix: engine modules (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac5, acceptance, already, apply, attempts (+123 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, already, apply, aware, back (+94 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: already, aware, back, build, cannot (+75 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mechanism): which of Options 1/2/3 should be implemented?** — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-22): Option 2** — commit `.pi/test-config.json` (stop ignoring it) so worktrees inherit it. Rationale: no cross-repo agent-framework change is required; the config is a repo-level fact and belongs in the repository.
- **Q2 (cross-repo execution/tracking): if a SorraAgents-side fix were needed, how should it be executed/tracked given `implement.py` has no `--worklog-dir` flag (so a run in SorraAgents targets the SorraAgents worklog, not this TCE item)?** — **Moot under Option 2.** The producer's standing preference (should a cross-repo fix be needed) is (a) a new SorraAgents work item with a `wl dep add` dependency, in preference to (b) reusing SA-0MTXLTKFP000ZUZ8. No SorraAgents change is in scope for this item, so no dependency is created.
- **Q3 (AC2/AC3 scope if Option 2): confirm AC2 is reworded to a TCE-side check and AC3's "implement skill" wording is dropped.** — **Confirmed (producer, 2026-09-22).** ACs 1–4 above reflect this: the regression test is a TCE-side tracked/not-ignored/present-in-worktree check, and documentation is scoped to `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-22 (plan): producer resolved the deferred Option choice (Option 2) and confirmed AC re-scoping; ACs rewritten to the tracked-config mechanism; no child work items required (pre-check `skip`: effort Small, risk Low).

## Failure Signature

- **Actual failing test file:** `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` (3 of 6 tests)
- Reported test name: `<suite exited 1>: npm --silent test` — generic triage signature, *not* a real test name
- Failing commit: 8b43c427123b713ae5a6ba3c27b2b1ba8f6dc310
- CI job: (not available)

### Failing tests (from the full-suite browser stage)

| # | Test | Observed failure |
|---|------|------------------|
| 1 | `advertises the +50% premium and makes the dragged upgrade follow the cursor` | `AssertionError: expected 328 to be greater than 348` — `container.x` never changed, so drag tracking never engaged |
| 2 | `dropping an upgrade on an eligible business buys and plays it at the premium` | `Timed out waiting for upgrade applied to the business after the drop` (10 s budget) |
| 3 | `animates the transfer from the drop location and plays the upgrade SFX` | `Timed out waiting for transfer animation to start after the drop` (30 s budget) |

## Verified Diagnosis (2026-09-22)

**Flaky under full-suite browser contention — not a code regression.**

Evidence gathered during planning:

1. **Unit stage is green.** `npx vitest run --project unit` → 381 files / 6709 tests passed (8 skipped).
2. **The file passes in isolation** at both the reported failing commit and current `dev`:
   `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` → 6/6 passed at `8b43c427` *and* at `139ff925`.
3. **The full browser suite passes on re-run.** `npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project browser` failed once (114 files, 3 failed) then passed on the next invocation (114 files / 657 tests, exit 0). The runner's retry-once guard does **not** cover this case: it retries only on Vitest's transient worker-RPC / browser-drop signatures, so a real per-test timeout is surfaced as a failure.
4. **Only drag-dependent tests fail.** The two tests in the file that do not require the pointer to actually track (`highlights eligible business slots green and ineligible ones red while dragging`, `rejects a drop on an ineligible business with a snap-back and no action spent`) passed in the same failing run. The three failures all require Phaser's game loop to process the drag gesture inside a fixed time window.

**Mechanism.** `beginDrag()` drives the gesture with fixed sleeps (`wait(40)` / `wait(60)` / `wait(80)`) after a 2×`requestAnimationFrame` wait. Phaser only flushes newly created interactive hit zones and processes queued pointer events during `InputPlugin.preUpdate` on the game-loop tick. Under full-suite Chromium contention (a `prepare` of ≈69 000 ms was observed in the failing run) that loop is starved, `dragstart` never fires, and the container never follows the pointer — so test 1's position assertion fails and tests 2/3 time out waiting for effects that depend on the drop.

## Precedent & Duplicate

- **Recurrence of CG-0MU0IV260002GHD7** ("browser full-suite contention flake (upgrade-drag-drop / HelpPanelLayering / expanded-viewport)"), closed `done` on 2026-09-14 with the disposition *"environmental flake, no code change warranted"*. That disposition is disproven by this recurrence — the same file is failing again two weeks later. The prior item also identified a concrete unapplied proposal: add `drainCanvasPool()` plus a settle delay to the Main Street browser `destroyGame` helpers, mirroring `tests/helpers/main-street-tutorial-e2e.ts`.
- **Related:** CG-0MU0RKGRC009Q1E6 (identical generic signature, closed `flaky` / non-reproducible on 2026-09-14).
- **In-repo precedent fix:** commit `da4290c8` ("harden expanded-viewport click-to-place against multi-instance contention") replaced a fixed-attempt gesture with an idempotent *retry-until-condition* loop bounded by a generous deadline, explicitly for this same contention class. That is the pattern to follow here.
- **Scope note:** `drainCanvasPool()` currently exists **only** in `tests/helpers/main-street-tutorial-e2e.ts` (~40 Main Street browser test files each carry their own `destroyGame` that does not drain the pool).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` passes under **full-suite browser load** (not only in isolation), verified by a green `npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project browser` run.
2. The drag gesture in that file no longer depends on fixed sleeps for the pointer to engage: it is driven by an idempotent retry-until-condition loop (or equivalent) with a generous deadline, while the regression guard is preserved — a genuinely broken drag/drop pipeline must still fail the test.
3. `npm test` (full suite: unit + browser + tutorial E2E) exits 0 at the fix commit.
4. `npm run build` is green.
5. Doc-update policy check: if the fix changes only test files it introduces no developer-workflow change, so no `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `AGENTS.md` update is required; if it touches any script, config, or structure, the docs are updated in the same commit.
6. The `flaky` tag is applied and a comment records the verified-green run (triage runbook step 2).

```

 ✓ |unit| tests/main-street/card-manifest.test.ts (2 tests) 25ms

# Coloretto: AI heuristic never takes a row proactively in round 1 (start-of-round passivity)

## Problem statement

During manual review of the ColorettoScene refactor (CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV) the producer reported: **"the AI never takes the action of 'take row' … previously when playing the game the AI would take a row to start scoring at some point during the round."**

The claim reproduces as a **heuristic-design limitation, not a refactor regression**:

- Over 200 seeded two-player games, the heuristic AI made **zero proactive takes in round 1** (156 takes were forced — all rows full / deck exhausted) and **911 proactive takes in rounds 2+**.
- Root cause: in round 1 every collection is empty. `netRowValue()` (``myGain − opponentsBestGain``) evaluates every row to **0** because each card is worth the same (+1) to every player, which is below `TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`. The AI therefore never takes until it is forced. Proactive takes only begin in round 2+, once the AI holds a persisted collection from a forced round-1 take.
- Secondary flaw: `marginalGain()` is summed per card against the player's *current* collection, so a row of 3 same-colour singles is valued at 3 rather than the true combined 6 — the heuristic cannot distinguish a 1-card row from a 3-card row.

This is **pre-existing** behaviour: `ColorettoAis.ts` has been byte-identical (modulo joker/bonus handling added in c87ae042) since the strategy was introduced in 00241c5f (CG-0MQH81B2Q001QFGY). The refactor commit fbac1a03 did not touch it, and a deterministic seeded replay is identical pre/post refactor.

## Users

- **Players** — expect the AI to contest rows and start building a collection early, not to place cards passively until forced.
- **Producers** — need the AI to feel like it is following the take-a-row rule during a round.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In round 1 (all collections empty) the heuristic AI takes a row proactively when that row is objectively strong (e.g. multiple cards of one colour), rather than only when every row is full.
2. The heuristic still avoids handing clearly strong rows to opponents (existing net-value behaviour retained).
3. `marginalGain`/row valuation accounts for the combined value of taking the whole row (a 3-same-colour row is valued ≈ its true 6 points, not 3).
4. New unit tests cover round-1 proactive takes and the combined-value valuation; existing `ColorettoAis` / `ColorettoGame` / `ColorettoScene` tests remain green.
5. `npm run build` succeeds; full unit suite (`npm test -- --project unit`) passes.

## Constraints

- Gameplay/AI change only — do **not** alter card rules, scoring, or the observer/scene rendering.
- Keep the change game-local (`example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts`); no engine promotion.
- Do not change `TAKE_THRESHOLD` semantics without evidence; prefer strengthening the row valuation and the take gate.

## Existing state / evidence

- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts` — `HeuristicStrategy`, `netRowValue`, `marginalGain`, `TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`.
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoGame.ts` — `dealRound()` persists collections across rounds (CG-0MSHWY9TT006GJY1), so round 1 is the only all-empty round.
- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoAis.test.ts` — the take tests all seed a non-empty collection, so round-1 passivity is currently untested.
- Seeded simulation evidence (200 two-player games): round-1 proactive = 0, forced = 156; rounds 2+ proactive = 911, forced = 197.

## Desired change

- Give the heuristic a positive reason to take a row in round 1 — e.g. take when the row's absolute value is high enough (using a correct whole-row valuation), while still subtracting opponent value to avoid feeding strong rows.
- Add tests for the round-1 take and the combined valuation.

## Related work

- **Discovered from:** CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV (Refactor: split ColorettoScene god class) — the producer's audit rejection that surfaced this.
- **Origin strategy item:** CG-0MQH81B2Q001QFGY (Coloretto AI strategies).
- **Collection-persistence item:** CG-0MSHWY9TT006GJY1 (negative colour scoring / collections persist).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Difficulty tuning (medium):** a more aggressive take gate changes game balance; pick a conservatively-scoped rule and validate with the existing deterministic AI tests.
- **Assumption:** the producer wants visible proactive AI takes during a round; if a different underlying regression was meant, this item should be re-scoped.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MLX1XQ7O189FC6H** – Transcript Recording (completed)
- **CG-0MQH80STI001DDAN** – Coloretto test suite (completed)
- **CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV** – Refactor: split ColorettoScene god class (1802 lines) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, add, added, alter (+153 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: absolute, acceptance, action, add, added (+124 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mqh81b2q001qfgy, 0mshwy9tt006gjy1, absolute, action, add (+114 more)

## Problem

Every Main Street card has a 64x64 art zone (at 8,8) containing a base64-encoded PNG sprite. When the card SVG is rasterised by Phaser at 4x quality scale, the 64x64 bitmap is upscaled 4x to fill a 256x256 device-pixel region, producing visible pixelation.

The 1024x1024 source sprites already exist in `example-games/main-street/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (commit 05026750, ~54 MB total). These are the original source art. Currently only `_64_x_64.png` files are used.

## Solution

1. Regenerate `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` to read `_1024_x_1024.png` source files and encode the embedded PNG at 256x256 (downsampled from 1024, with 256-colour palette encoding).
2. Regenerate `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` and all `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` files.
3. Keep `GRAPHIC_W/H = 64` in the SVG layout (the art zone stays 64x64 CSS pixels, the higher-resolution bitmap is simply downsampled crisply during rasterisation).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 63 `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files are used as sources (not `_64_x_64.png`)
2. Embedded PNGs in `card-art-map.json` are 256x256 (verified by parsing data URI and checking decoded dimensions)
3. All SVGs in `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` embed the 256x256 art
4. Unit tests pass (`npm test -- --project unit`)
5. Build succeeds (`npm run build`)
6. Visual verification: card art zone is no longer pixelated at 1x, 2x, and 3x viewport scale

## Files to modify

- `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` - source suffix, encoding dimensions
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` - regenerated
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` - regenerated via SVG generator
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` - CARD_ART_SIZE stays 64 (unchanged)
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` - update test expectations if any
